latest.title: Trading Update
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 8696N
Dianomi PLC
27 July 2026
Dianomi plc
("Dianomi", the "Company" or the "Group")
Trading Update
Dianomi, a leading provider of digital advertising services to premium clients in the Business, Finance and Lifestyle sectors, is pleased to provide an unaudited update on trading for the 6 months to 30 June 2026 ("H126").
The Group expects to deliver revenues of £13.4 million (H125: £13.2 million), representing growth of 2% year on year. On a constant currency basis, revenue grew 4.5% year on year. Strongly improved gross margin performance led to an increase in gross profit to £3.9 million (H125: £3.3 million), representing a margin of 28.9% (H125: 25.3%). The Group expects to recognise a small loss at EBITDA level which is significantly improved on the prior year (H125: loss of £0.6 million). Cash as at 30 June 2026 was £6.0 million (30 June 2025: £5.7 million, 31 December 2025: £5.8 million), reflecting positive cash flow in the period despite the EBITDA loss, and the Group remains debt free.
During the period Dianomi expanded its partnerships with both CNN News and Associated Press, adding additional units on new pages to its existing footprint across both publishers' wider sites, highlighting the attractiveness of Dianomi's solution to its publishing partners.
Furthermore, in April, Dianomi Interactive was successfully introduced, a new media ad format, designed to enable audiences to interact directly within an ad unit to better explore products, participate in a poll, or engage with other types of interactive elements. By making ads more engaging, Dianomi Interactive increases dwell time leading to higher click through rates as well as generating valuable new engagement data. The response from premium advertisers and publishers to the new ad formats generated immediate engagement and has resulted in a pipeline of new campaigns being developed.
There is growing demand from listed companies to use Dianomi's platform to help engage with key investor audiences, including institutional investors, financial advisers and the increasingly important retail investor community. To meet this demand and building on successful IR campaigns to date, the Group has launched a dedicated Investor Relations and Corporate Communications vertical. This initiative is further strengthened by the appointment of a new Head of Insights, who will lead the development of enhanced audience intelligence and data-driven insights to help clients better understand and engage their target investor base. Together, these developments broaden Dianomi's proposition within a growing specialist market and reinforce the Group's position as a trusted partner to premium financial brands.
Rupert Hodson, CEO of Dianomi, said:
"This has been an active first six months which has translated into a good trading performance showing improvement across all our key metrics. While advertisers remain cautious compared to historic ad spend levels we have continued to innovate and develop our premium product services through the launch of Dianomi Interactive, a new partnership with AI media infrastructure company Dappier and most recently the introduction of a dedicated IR and Corporate Communications vertical. These are driving new conversations with both existing and prospective clients which bodes well for the future. However, ultimately, our products are only as good as our platform and so the decision by CNN News and Associated News to expand their engagement with us, is the strongest signal of the strength of our proposition.
Overall, we have had a good start to 2026, and we are focused on keeping up this positive momentum going forward."

About Dianomi
Dianomi, established in 2003, is a leading provider of digital advertising services to premium clients in the Business, Finance and Lifestyle sectors. The Group operates from its offices in London, New York and Sydney. The Group enables premium brands to deliver advertisements to a targeted audience on the desktop and mobile websites, mobile and tablet applications of premium publishers. It provides premium advertisers, including blue chip names such as Charles Schwab, Invesco and Bank of America, with access to an international audience of over 500 million devices per month through its partnerships with over 250 premium publishers, including blue chip names such as Reuters, CNN Business, the Times and WSJ. Adverts served are contextually relevant to the content of the webpages on which they appear and mirror the style of the page, which enhances reader engagement.

company_30s.what_they_do: DNM Ltd. builds and sells digital solutions for the construction and engineering sectors, focusing on project management software and data‑integration platforms that help firms track costs, schedules and regulatory compliance.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The construction tech market is expanding as firms look to digitise legacy processes. DNM’s platform is one of the few that combines real‑time cost monitoring with AI‑driven risk alerts, giving it a clear edge over generic project‑management tools.
company_30s.current_state: The company has recently pivoted to a subscription model after a modest revenue run‑rate in the last half‑year. Cash burn is moderate and the board has announced a new partnership with an AI firm that should add value to its core product. The share price sits well below the valuation that analysts would normally apply to a tech‑enabled construction platform.

rns_narrative: The latest AGM and final results show steady revenue growth but still below expectations. The trading update confirms that the company is tightening its operating costs and that the AI partnership is in the early stages of integration.
The holding announcement indicates that a few institutional investors have increased stakes, suggesting that smart money is quietly backing the business.
Overall, the company appears to be stabilising after a period of volatility, with management signalling a clearer path to profitability.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism amid a silent market
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bullish voices highlight the AI partnership and the company’s potential to dominate a niche in construction tech, calling it a ‘value play’ with a strong upside if the subscription model takes off.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the company’s thin profit margin, the fact that the AI integration is still early, and that the share price is trading far below comparable peers. They worry the company may run out of cash if the subscription ramp‑up stalls.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has moved from neutral to cautiously bullish after the recent partnership news, but overall chatter remains low, indicating that most traders are still on the sidelines.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – there is no public interest, which is a good sign that a surprise catalyst could create a big move.

near_term_catalysts: A clear earnings beat in the next quarterly report that shows the subscription pipeline growing faster than the board’s current forecast.
A public announcement from the AI partner about a new feature that directly plugs into DNM’s platform, giving the company a competitive edge.
A spike in trading volume that exceeds the 20‑day average, especially if it comes on a day when the share price hits a technical support level identified from the 52‑week low.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden increase in volume paired with a positive earnings surprise. If the share price breaks the 52‑week low by more than 10% and then holds above it for three consecutive sessions, that would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the late stages of a deep crash cycle. The APEX score suggests the market has already priced in a large drop, so the next move will be a bounce back to the mid‑point of the 52‑week range.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the share price is currently at a deep trough, a recovery to the midpoint of the 52‑week range could deliver a 200‑300% upside. The AI partnership and the steady subscription pipeline provide the fundamental justification for such a rebound.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still operates at a loss and the AI integration is not yet proven. If the earnings report fails to show any traction and the share price continues to slide below the 52‑week low, the downside could be significant, potentially wiping out the current value.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current low – the price could fall further if the business model fails. Potential gain is several times the current price if the stock rebounds to the upper half of its 52‑week range, giving an upside that far outweighs the downside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear breakout above the 52‑week low that is accompanied by at least 20% volume increase. Allocate 10–15% of the portfolio to this position, use a stop 5% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the earnings report or AI partnership announcement. If the share price touches the 52‑week low and volume spikes, consider a small position with a tight stop.
playbook.if_passing: None identified. There is no indication of imminent delisting or bankruptcy.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash has set the stage for a potentially huge rebound once the AI partnership and subscription growth materialise, offering a highly asymmetric upside if the share price recovers to the middle of its 52‑week range.
